title: Sortie ledger
overseerSummary: Records the killer and fight of each fall, keeps the last 8 sortie reports, and counts sent/won/lost per contract type on the board. Facts only; no sentence infers a cause.

proposals.title: Record the cause of each fall and a per-type result, then keep the last 8 sortie reports
proposals.problem: The Field is the main content and leaves nothing behind. The log is in memory, 'Back to the board' discards it, and the only record is one game-log line. Per-fight blocks are already computed and then thrown away. A player who loses a squad cannot tell whether the cause was the ground, a boss, a missing support role or the contract type, and the memorial says only the mission name. The contract card's payout multiplier does not track risk: measured over 15 contract types on combat.js, deaths per sortie range from 0.01 (escort) to 1.26 (assassination) and the correlation between the multiplier and deaths is +0.54 while the correlation between the multiplier and win rate is -0.26.
evidence: bestiary.js:95-106 Bestiary.record pushes per-fight blocks onto the run it is given (enemies with id, icon, level, hp, maxHp, dealt, attacks; party rows with hp, maxHp, dealt, taken, healed, attacks, crits, dodges, parries, casts, techniques, potions, conditions; kills with killer; last 40 log lines); sortie.js:177 passes the sortie's run

sortie.js:299-302 persist() saves id, party, loot, zone, started and the field state only; run.encounters, run.teamId, run.teamName and run.bonus are not saved. sortie.js:439-541 settle() copies nothing into state; sortie.js:1281 'Back to the board' sets run = null

report.js:20-73 renderRun/encounterBlock read run.mission (falls back to {icon, name: run.mission} when the id is not in Missions.MISSION), run.result, run.lost, run.rewards, run.loot, run.encounters; encounterBlock needs enemy id/icon/hp/maxHp/attacks/dealt and party hp/maxHp/attacks/crits/dodges/parries/casts/potions/conditions and e.log. A compact record without those fields cannot be drawn by it.

game.js:2346-2360 the only caller of Report.renderRun, for Gate runs; missions.js (finish) stores state.missions.history.slice(0, 20) with full encounters, so the save already carries 20 full run reports

combat.js:158 logs '<name> falls (<source>)' and calls ctx.onDeath(target, attacker); combat.js:618 onDeath records enemy kills only (kills.push) and drops party falls; combat.js onDeath has these two sites only
roster.js:87-105 memorial cause is whatever the caller passes; sortie.js:450 passes m.name; game.js:1628 matches cause.startsWith('sacrificed to'), so a mission cause may be extended
sortie.js:768-787 missionCard shows label, level, party, blurb, brief, win terms, exit, side jobs, twists and the payout tag; no prior result

MEASURED, combat.js runner (15 types, 180 sorties each across three roster tiers): siege win 17% / 1.04 deaths per sortie / x2.13; dungeon 45% / 0.84 / x2.14; raid 47% / 0.71 / x3.19; assassination 67% / 1.26 / x2.65; capture 88% / 0.12 / x2.69; extermination 86% / 0.09 / x1.08; hold 50% / 0.08 / x1.63; survival 48% / 0.09 / x1.61; expedition 89% / 0.08 / x1.38; escort 100% / 0.01 / x1.64; corr(multiplier, deaths per sortie) = +0.54, corr(multiplier, win rate) = -0.26 (multiplier = mean MT.roll reward at level 3, 200 rolls)

MEASURED, stored size of the real Bestiary.record blocks over 300 sorties: mean 9.5 KB per sortie (p50 7.8, p90 15.7, max 72 KB; about 1.6 KB per fight; p50 5 fights, max 47); without the log field mean 7.0 KB
field.js:105-109 and field.js:1993 the field log is {t, text} lines, 300 kept in the save; sortie.js:554 treats lines starting with two spaces as combat detail
proposals.change:
Part A (S, ships with loop-retreat):
1. combat.js: ctx.onDeath(target, attacker, source) at line 158 and, in encounter() at line 618, else-branch for party deaths: falls.push({ id: t.char ? t.char.id : null, name: t.name, by: killer ? killer.name : null, source }); return falls with the result. Bestiary.record copies res.falls into the encounter block as falls.
2. sortie.js settle(): look the fallen character up in the run's falls and pass cause: '<mission name>: <killer name>' (or the mission name alone when the killer is unknown) to Roster.fall at sortie.js:450. Roster.fall itself is edited only by loop-record. Memorial cards (sortie.js:1096-1126) show the cause; killer names resolve through Bestiary.knowledge so a species the town has not met stays masked.
3. sortie.js settle(): gs.field.types[type] = { sent, won, dead }, incremented once per settled run. missionCard (sortie.js:768) adds 'your record: N sent, N won, N lost' when sent > 0, and nothing else on that line (counts of things the player did).
Part B (M):
4. sortie.js resolve(): after Bestiary.record, annotate the pushed block: enc.width = opts.frontage, enc.startHp = average HP fraction of ours before the fight (computed before C.encounter).
5. persist() (sortie.js:299) also saves run.encounters, capped at the last 12, so a reload does not drop the early fights.
6. settle(): unshift onto gs.field.history (cap 8) a run-shaped record: { id, mission: m.name, result: s.result.why, type, level, at, party: [{id, name}], lost: [names], rewards: paid, loot: [{kind:'gems', amount}], encounters: last 12 blocks, with e.log kept only for blocks where a party member fell and set to [] elsewhere }. Because it has the shape report.js already reads, Report.renderRun(container, record, state, M) draws it unchanged. report.js changes: skip the 'blow by blow' details element when e.log is empty, and print falls ('Bram fell to a Goblin Warrior').
7. Board: a collapsible 'Reports' box (collapsible key 'reports', sortie.js:588 pattern) with one button per record. 'Back to the board' opens the newest. Under the report, 'What decided it' lists recorded facts only: the result string; the first fight in which a member fell with its enemies (names via Bestiary.knowledge), ground width (enc.width mapped by F.groundWord) and the squad's average HP at its start; the roles present (Outfit.roleOf). No sentence infers a cause.
8. Measure localStorage size before and after on a save with 60 characters; budget: 8 records at about 7 KB mean is about 56 KB, bounded at 8 x 12 blocks.
proposals.playerEffect: After a loss the player reads which fight killed whom, on what ground, with what HP at its start, and changes one thing before the next launch. The contract board gives an evidence base the multiplier does not: the town's own count of sent, won and lost per type. With measured deaths per sortie differing by a factor of 100 between types, this is the lever that replaces the free undo.
proposals.secondOrder: Feeds loop-record (the same settle() pass fills per-character counters) and gives loop-wounds and loop-retreat a place to explain themselves ('dropped to 18% HP', 'called back'). Bestiary tiers become readable in context (a report row can show how much of a species the town knows). The memorial gains a cause with a killer. The per-type record gives the board a feedback loop without changing payouts. Persisting run.encounters means the Field run and Gate runs share one report shape.
proposals.risks: State size: 8 records at about 7 KB mean is about 56 KB, p90 sortie 12 KB, worst case bounded by the 12-block cap (about 20 KB each); the Gate already stores 20 full reports (missions.js history slice 20), so this is the same class of storage. Measure on a real save. The per-type counts are small samples early on (a line shown after one sortie says little); the card prints counts only. Report.renderRun reads Bestiary.knowledge per enemy, so unknown species stay masked; check that a record outlives a species being renamed (it stores id and name). persist() saving encounters adds to the live save: at most 12 blocks (about 20 KB). Payout retuning is not proposed: the type table comes from plain characters without gear, so it supports showing the player their own record, not changing multipliers.
proposals.response: Engineering attack (record and renderer disagree; 3 KB per fight so 20 runs is 300+ KB): confirmed against report.js:25-73. Reworked to store run-shaped records the renderer already draws. Size re-measured on the real Bestiary.record output: about 1.6 KB per fight, 9.5 KB mean per sortie, 7.0 KB without logs; 8 records with logs kept only for fights with a fall comes to about 56 KB, not 300 KB. Cap lowered from 20 to 8. Engineering demand 2 (per-type record and memorial cause ship first as S): done as part A, shipped with the retreat. Demand 3 (named stored fields for 'what decided it'): listed. Demand 4 (measure on a 60-character save): specified as step 8. Design attack (reading material, may never be opened): the per-type card line changes a decision without opening anything, which is why it is part A. Design demand (ids and counts only, no inferring sentence, cap 10, killer names through Bestiary.knowledge, card line 'N sent, N won, N lost' only, Roster.fall edit shared with loop-record): ids and counts only, facts-only block, cap 8, masking kept, card line as stated, and Roster.fall's body is now edited only in loop-record while this proposal only changes the cause string at the call site.

verdicts.attack: It is reading material, not a mechanic: a player who Skips every run may never open it, and the 'What decided it' block is one sentence away from telling the player something false. Twenty records at 2-3 KB is about 50 KB of localStorage beside a save already at 3 KB per character. The per-type record is the only part that changes a decision (which contract), and it works without the rest.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: Bestiary.record builds encounter blocks on the run (bestiary.js:95-106) and sortie.js:177 passes the sortie run; persist() stores id, party, loot, zone, started, state only (sortie.js:299-302); 'Back to the board' sets run = null (sortie.js:1281); Report.renderRun is called only at game.js:2360 for Gate runs and falls back on a name string (report.js:26); combat.js:618 onDeath records enemy kills only; memorial cause is m.name (sortie.js:450, roster.js:97); game.js:1628 matches cause with startsWith('sacrificed to'). My POW 0.6 harness run reproduces the win-rate spread by type (raid 21%, dungeon 29-36%, extermination and escort 100%) against card multipliers that do not follow it.
verdicts.demand: Records hold ids and counts only. The 'what decided it' block lists facts (the fight of the first fall, its enemies, ground width, squad HP at start) and contains no sentence that infers a cause. Cap at 10 records and report save size before and after. Killer names resolve through Bestiary.knowledge so an unmet species stays masked. The per-type card line is 'N sent, N won, N lost' and nothing else. Roster.fall's cause change shares an owner with loop-record's edit of the same function.

verdicts.attack: The record and the renderer disagree. Report.renderRun/encounterBlock (report.js:25-73) reads run.encounters with party rows carrying hp, maxHp, attacks, crits, dodges, parries, casts, potions, conditions and enemy rows carrying id, icon, maxHp, hp, dealt, attacks; the proposed compact record (party[{id,name,alive,low,dealt,taken,healed,casts,potions,kills}], fights[{enemies[{name,level,alive}],...}]) has none of those, so renderRun cannot draw it. Storing the Bestiary.record blocks instead (bestiary.js:95-106, 40 log lines per fight) is roughly 3 KB per fight, so a six-fight run is 15-20 KB and 20 runs are 300+ KB in localStorage beside a save measured at 3 KB per character. The 2-3 KB estimate is for the record the renderer cannot read.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified bestiary.js:95-106 builds per-fight blocks on the run passed from sortie.js:177; persist() (sortie.js:299-302) saves id, party, loot, zone, started, state only; 'Back to the board' sets run = null (sortie.js:1281); game.js:2360 is the only Report.renderRun caller; combat.js:618 onDeath pushes enemy kills only and combat.js:158 logs falls; field.js:1993 keeps 300 log lines; roster.js:95-105 memorial fields; game.js:1628 uses startsWith('sacrificed to'). Harness win-rate-by-type table not re-run; my 6-run baseline shows the same shape (raid 0%, siege 17%, capture 100%).
verdicts.demand: 1) Pick one: store the full encounters array and cap history at about 8 with a measured size, or store the compact record and write a compact renderer that does not call Report.renderRun. 2) The per-type record and the memorial cause '<mission>: <by>' are fine as specified and can ship first as an S. 3) 'What decided it' is built only from named stored fields; list them. 4) Measure localStorage size before and after on a 60-character save.
